note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LONG TAPERED BRISTLEGRASS HEAD
tiles.details: A coarse perennial with culms ~60–120 cm and often 5–18 mm broad blades. Flowering head roughly 15–25 cm in FNA/Kew, up to ~35 cm in Texas A&M. Existing image indices 0–1 show public-reusable broad architecture; original CC BY-NC image is held outside the public gallery and retains its existing rights hold.
tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: tall perennial with broad often hairy leaves and loose tapering bottlebrush
tiles.status: ACTUAL HEAD PHOTO — SAME-PLANT ROOTED HABIT NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · SHORT HAIR-FRINGE LIGULE
tiles.details: Williamson County treatment describes a tiny truncate ciliate membrane, often <0.5 mm; FNA/GrassBase describes a roughly 1–2 mm hairy/fringed ligule. These may emphasize different portions of the collar. Expose the inner blade/sheath junction with 1-mm scale, document membrane and hairs separately, and never substitute hairy stem nodes for a ligule. Existing photographs do not prove the exact dimensions.
tiles.short: Open the inner collar: distinguish a minute ciliate membrane from adjacent longer hairs

tiles.heading: 03 · MOSTLY ONE LONG BASAL BRISTLE
tiles.details: Long projecting structures are sterile branchlets, NOT floret lemma awns. Several bristles are obvious in gross flowering photos, but actual number and insertion at one ~2.2–2.5 mm spikelet are unresolved. Photograph multiple attached ripe units at 10–20× with ruler; do not infer a universal count from a distant head.
tiles.short: Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) persistent bristles per spikelet, about 10–35 mm

tiles.heading: 04 · TINY 2.2–2.5 MM SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Regional treatment reports mature spikelets ~2.2–2.5 mm. Lower glume roughly half spikelet length, 3-veined; upper glume roughly 3/4 to near fertile lemma length, 5-veined. These are treatment-relative proportions, not direct measurements from the archived head photos.
tiles.short: Inspect one ripe spikelet beside 1-mm scale, not a long bristle mistaken for the floret

tiles.heading: 05 · FIRM FINELY WRINKLED UPPER LEMMA
tiles.details: Lower sterile lemma commonly 5-veined; a shorter lower palea may be present. Firm upper fertile lemma has fine transverse wrinkles, without a long true lemma awn. To demonstrate this, photograph a mature ~2.2–2.5 mm spikelet opened to show lower/upper glumes, sterile lemma/palea and fertile lemma.
tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma ~fertile lemma length; upper fertile lemma hard, cross-wrinkled and unawned

tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK REVERCHON AND KNOTROOT
tiles.details: S. reverchonii has a narrower often interrupted head and sparse ~2–8 mm bristles where present; S. parviflora generally 4–12 bristles per spikelet and knotty rhizomes; S. italica is a dense-headed annual. Limestone canyon habitat is supportive only, never proof of taxon or Hays native status. Compare measured ripe attachments and the true collar.
tiles.short: Mostly solitary 10–35 mm bristles versus sparse short S. reverchonii and many-bristled S. parviflora
tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED REPRODUCTIVE MACROS NEEDED

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START with the Kyla Miller archived photo: locate the long tapered flowering axis and conspicuous long outward projecting bristles. The three existing arrows mark visible gross structures, not counted spikelet attachments.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Williamson County treatment describes a tiny truncate ciliate membrane, often <0.5 mm; FNA/GrassBase describes a roughly 1–2 mm hairy/fringed ligule. These may emphasize different portions of the collar. Expose the inner blade/sheath junction with 1-mm scale, document membrane and hairs separately, and never substitute hairy stem nodes for a ligule. Existing photographs do not prove the exact dimensions.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Regional treatment reports mature spikelets ~2.2–2.5 mm. Lower glume roughly half spikelet length, 3-veined; upper glume roughly 3/4 to near fertile lemma length, 5-veined. These are treatment-relative proportions, not direct measurements from the archived head photos.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Conspicuously projecting mostly solitary ~10–35 mm bristles on an elongate tapered head distinguish S. scheelei from sparse/shorter-bristled interrupted S. reverchonii and the many-bristled short rhizomatous S. parviflora. Annual foxtail millet S. italica can have a long head but usually denser/lobed cultivated seedheads, broad foliage and nonperennial roots. Check at least several mature spikelets; bristles are sterile branches, NOT awns.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

The original source identification is retained without claiming a Hays County voucher.

panels.label: UVALDE COUNTY · living plant in Dry Frio rocky gulley habitat
panels.caption: Jim Conrad photographed actual Southwestern/Scheele's bristlegrass beside the Dry Frio River in northern Uvalde County in September 2013. Look for slender tapered flowering heads attached to leafy culms in rocky, partly shaded habitat. Multiple grasses share the scene: do not infer that every green blade belongs to this one specimen. The root system and true ligule are hidden.

panels.caption: Original Jim Conrad close photograph of the same north-Uvalde Setaria scheelei population: elongated pale-green spikelets sit on a branched axis with many long threadlike projecting bristles. The bristles are reduced sterile branchlets, not lemma awns. These clear structures help crew compare foxtails. No 1-mm scale or peeled ligule is present; do NOT derive numerical length or exact per-spikelet bristle counts from this image.

intro: SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.
memory_rule: MILLET=ANNUAL HEAVY HEAD (usually 1–3 bristles); PARVIFLORA=KNOTTY RHIZOME + MANY (4–12); REVERCHONII=INTERRUPTED SPARSE (2–8 mm where bristled); SCHEELEI=LONG SINGLE (10–35 mm).
safety_note: 3 exact-source JPEGs are listed in the canonical species gallery. Gaiacoyote's 154,130-byte 800×592 CC0 overview was independently byte- and pixel-checked and has three gross-organ arrows; the separate Annika Lindqvist JPEG could not be byte-inspected in this run. No authenticated close-up proves bristle number per spikelet, glume veins, or 1–2-mm ligule. Existing CC BY-NC and all original source records preserved; source-page live license recheck for Gaiacoyote remains pending. PUBLIC RIGHTS NOTE 2026-10-25: CC BY-NC original is held from the public site; its 3 gross-organ arrows are preserved under visual_comparison.rights_held_comparison_items. Public same-species gallery now begins with 2 already archived CC0/CC BY originals; true measured anatomy remains missing.
field_rule: LONG conspicuous projecting mostly solitary bristles + relatively loose tapered foxtail panicle + hairy broad leaves; confirm the SINGLE bristle attachment and tiny hair-fringed ligule.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.

Annual foxtail millet S. italica can have a long head but usually denser/lobed cultivated seedheads, broad foliage and nonperennial roots. Check at least several mature spikelets; bristles are sterile branches, NOT awns.
